Research Interests

  Study physics in solid-state materials: how defects & quasiparticles affect their electrical and optical properties.
  Analyze defect states and local structure with transient spectroscopy (PICTS/DLTS) and tip-enhanced nanospectroscopy.
  Develop and apply interpretable machine learning to extract physically meaningful information from experimental data.

Research
1. Defect Physics in Solid-State Materials

  Defect states in oxide semiconductors and their relation to device characteristics and stability. (Surf. Interfaces 2025; Sci. Rep. 2023; IEEE Trans. Electron Devices 2024; ACS Appl. Electron. Mater. 2024)
  Defect-mediated control of carrier type in 2D semiconductors for complementary devices.
  Exciton modulation in 2D semiconductors through coupling to plasmonic nanostructures.

2. Defect and Nanoscale Spectroscopy

  Transient spectroscopy (PICTS/DLTS) of defect states in 2D semiconductors.
  Nanoscale mapping of defects and strain in 2D materials by tip-enhanced spectroscopy.
  Electromagnetic simulation of near-field enhancement in tip-enhanced spectroscopy. (Mater. Des. 2026)

3. Interpretable AI for Science

  Interpretable machine learning relating Raman spectra to electrical properties.
  Deep-learning noise reduction of experimental spectra that preserves spectral parameters.
  Simulation of analog in-memory learning based on measured synaptic characteristics of ferroelectric InSe neuromorphic devices.
  Numerical precision and the reliability of scientific machine learning. (ICML 2026)
  Review of the physical interpretability of machine-learning analysis in spectroscopy.
